Keywords: Witnesses to Visby debts across distance
RagShortTexts: Visby merchants used partners, accounts and debt across distances.
Less carried silver did not remove repayment or the need to identify debtors and due dates.

Variants.Content: Visby merchants used partners, accounts and debt to trade over distance without carrying all silver on every journey. Claims required identifiable creditors, debtors and due dates, with accounts, witnesses and a place of recourse when disputed.

Visby merchants used partners, accounts and debt to trade over distance without carrying all silver on every journey. Claims required identifiable creditors, debtors and due dates, with accounts, witnesses and a place of recourse when disputed. Carriers needed recipients, acknowledgments and replies. Delays disrupted due accounts, while private commissions still needed mounts, lodging and guards.

Visby merchants used partners, accounts and debt to trade over distance without carrying all silver on every journey. Claims required identifiable creditors, debtors and due dates, with accounts, witnesses and a place of recourse when disputed. Merchants broadened exchange through partners but tracked debts and recourse. One vessel or partner holding all capital exposed later promises to a single failure.

Visby merchants used partners, accounts and debt to trade over distance without carrying all silver on every journey. Claims required identifiable creditors, debtors and due dates, with accounts, witnesses and a place of recourse when disputed. Small traders supported families while owing goods; unsold stock meant little cash and food. Familiar trust helped, but guarantors faced neighborhood pressure when payment failed.
